title: Catalog entry pinflow: interaction cases and microcopy sketches
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working sketch for the model-catalog -> endpoint creation -> model version pinning interaction. The goal is to capture realistic microcopy, alternative interaction cases (happy path, low-confidence model, fallback variant, version-skew warning), error messages, and a short backlog of follow-ups. This is intentionally lightweight and written as a companion to the quick wires (see linked PR) rather than a final spec.

Audience:
- Console PMs and designers (review & iterate)
- Frontend engineers implementing the pin modal and endpoint creator
- Solutions engineers who will demo the flows to customers

Assumptions:
- Users can choose a model variant (e.g., gptx-10b-fp16, gptx-10b-q4) from the catalog card or within endpoint creation.
- Pinning binds an endpoint route to a model version (immutable reference) until explicitly rolled back or repinned.
- There are lightweight compatibility checks (tokenizer, sequence length, and kv-cache support) that run in the background.

High level UX goals:
1) Make pinning low-friction for PLG users (clear defaults, one-click quick pin).
2) Surface critical safety/compatibility warnings early (nonblocking but visible).
3) Provide clear rollback and fallback copy so ops teams understand risk and recovery.
4) Keep microcopy consistent with Console tone: concise, action-focused, and reassuring.

Interaction cases and sketches (wireframe references):
- Case A: Quick pin from catalog card (happy path)
  - Trigger: user sees model card, clicks "Quick pin to new endpoint"
  - Modal: title "Create endpoint & pin model"; sections: Endpoint name (auto-suggest), Route path (auto /api/{name}), Model (preselected), Version (immutable once pinned), Region selector.
  - Primary action copy: "Create endpoint and pin"; Secondary: "Create without pinning (advanced)"
  - Microcopy under version label: "Pinned to v2025-01-06. To pick a different version, choose Advanced."
  - Success toast: "Endpoint created — model pinned. Traffic routed to v2025-01-06."

- Case B: Advanced pin with variant selection and quantization note
  - Additional toggles: hardware preference, quantization profile suggestion (recommended), KV cache enabled checkbox.
  - Inline help copy for quantization: "Quantized variant may reduce cost by ~40% at similar quality for short prompts."
  - Danger copy if user picks a less tested variant: "Experimental variant — expect occasional regressions. Enable canary routing to test with a subset of traffic."

- Case C: Compatibility check fails (tokenizer mismatch or unsupported kv-cache)
  - Inline error state: red banner at top of modal: "Model variant \"gptx-10b-legacy-tokenizer\" is incompatible with endpoint config: tokenizer v2 required."
  - Actions offered: "Choose compatible variant" (primary) and "Proceed anyway (advanced)" (secondary, requires confirmation).
  - Confirmation copy dialog: "Proceeding may produce unexpected tokenization differences and can affect generation quality. Proceed?"

- Case D: Low-confidence stability check (non-blocking)
  - Yellow banner: "This model variant has limited stability data for long generation (>2048 tokens). Consider enabling fallback to a stable variant."
  - Suggested CTA: "Enable fallback" -> opens small rule-editor to pick fallback variant and traffic percentage.

- Case E: Existing endpoint re-pin attempt (warn about freeze)
  - If user attempts to pin a new version to an endpoint already pinned: modal title "Update pin for endpoint 'chat-agent'"
  - Warning line: "Updating the pinned version will change outputs for all current clients that rely on this route."
  - Suggested mitigations (checkboxes): run canary (10% traffic), schedule rollout window, create snapshot test.
  - Button copy: "Update pin (start canary)"; small muting: "If you need a zero-diff deploy, use 'Create new endpoint' instead."

Microcopy library (draft strings)
- Primary CTAs:
  - Create endpoint and pin
  - Pin version
  - Update pin (start canary)
  - Create without pinning
  - Enable fallback

- Helper / inline notes:
  - Pinned versions are immutable. To change outputs without downtime, create a new endpoint or run a canary rollout.
  - Recommended: pick the verified variant for lowest regression risk.
  - Quantized variants reduce cost, may slightly change output.

- Error & warning lines:
  - Model variant incompatible with selected endpoint config.
  - Tokenizer mismatch detected — use a compatible variant or enable advanced token mapping.
  - Limited stability data for long contexts (>2048 tokens). Consider a fallback.
  - Variant is experimental; enable canary routing for safe rollout.

- Tooltips and micro-interactions:
  - (i) Info icon next to "Version": "Pin binds this endpoint to a specific model snapshot. Pins are immutable unless updated."
  - (ii) Hover on quantization suggestion: "Estimated cost: -42% tokens/cycle. Quality impact: small for short prompts."
  - (iii) Small success chip: "Pinned: v2025-01-06 — canary 0%"

Error messaging guidelines (developer-facing)
- Keep errors actionable: always include the problem and the next step. E.g., "Tokenizer mismatch — choose variant X or enable token-mapping in advanced config."
- Avoid vague language like "Something went wrong" on modal. Reserve for unexpected backend failures and provide a retry.
- Use consistent severity colors and short banners: red = blocking, amber = caution, blue = info.

Backlog items / TODOs
- [ ] Add audit note copy for pinned changes (what appears in endpoint timeline). Ticket: RED-4722
- [ ] Wire up canary traffic perc slider in the modal (UX + API contract). RED-4723
- [ ] Add unit tests for failure-to-pin flows (auth, quota exhausted). RED-4724
- [ ] Small visual: micro-anim for pin success (pin icon -> chip) to reassure users. Design spike.
- [ ] Design copy variants for enterprise vs self-serve (more explicit safeguards for enterprise).

Open questions / decisions needed
- 1) Should "Create without pinning" still allow users to preselect a version for later pinning? Pros: convenience. Cons: confusion about default routing.
- 2) Exact wording for immutable pin: do we say "immutable" or "version-locked"? Ops feedback: "immutable" is stronger but might alarm new users.
- 3) Do we allow "proceed anyway" for incompatible tokenizer by default, or gate it behind an enterprise flag? Security teams prefer gating.

Notes to engineers:
- API contract: endpoint.create should accept model_version_id and optional fallback_variant with canary_percent. If compatibility check fails, return structured errors with codes: COMPAT_TOKENIZER, COMPAT_KV_CACHE, STABILITY_LOW.
- Frontend should treat COMPAT_* as non-blocking warnings except COMPAT_TOKENIZER which is blocking by default. This behavior can be toggled via feature-flag.

Sample acceptance criteria (MVP)
- User can quick-pin from a model card and immediately see the endpoint listed with a pinned-version label.
- Attempt to pin an incompatible tokenizer variant shows a blocking error and prevents creation.
- Updating a pin surfaces the rollout options (canary) and requires explicit confirmation for direct full-rollout.
- Success toast and endpoint timeline entry exist for pin actions.

Notes to self (formatting & future):
- Move final microcopy strings to i18n keys: console.pinflow.*
- Coordinate with solutions eng to capture a set of verified variants to mark as "recommended" in the catalog.
- Follow up with SRE on implications of auto-fallback (cost, cache invalidation).

References and links:
- Quick wires in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/780
- Compatibility checks service design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ARCH/compatibility-checks
- Related backlog ticket: RED-4567
